name: Icon Button
summary: An icon button is a button drawn as a glyph with no words on it. Use it where a label would not fit: a toolbar, a table row, the corner of a panel. Because there is no visible text, the accessible name is the only name the button has, and it is the thing most often left out.
demoNote: Every example under Common mistakes is live. The readout under each button says where its name came from, or that it has none.

contract.useWhen: A button whose only label is an attribute, at a size a finger can hit.
keyboard: native: one stop, the same as any button. The glyph is aria-hidden and takes none
failureModes: no name at all, so it announces as a bare button
the aria-label on the wrapper instead of on the button
a visible word left out of the name (SC 2.5.3 Label in Name)
shrink-wrapped to the glyph, under the 24px floor (SC 2.5.8)
the SVG left in the name, which gives it a second and worse half
